title: Steam News - Steam Families is here - Steam News
snippet:
Steam Families includes new parental controls that allow parents to set limits on what and when children play games on Steam. You can control which games your children have access to and monitor their activity. This information is available from wherever you access Steam, including your mobile device when you are away from home. [...] Of course! Let's say that you are in a family with 4 members and that you own a copy of Portal 2 and a copy of Half-Life. At any time, any one member can play Portal 2 and another can play Half-Life. If two of you would like to play Portal 2 at the same time, someone else in the family will need to purchase a copy of the game. After that purchase, there are two owned copies of Portal 2 across the family and any two members can play at the same time. [...] ## Family Sharing

When you join a Steam Family, you automatically gain access to the shareable games that your family members own and they will also be able to access the shareable titles in your library. The next time you log in to Steam, this new 'family library' will appear in the left column as a subsection of your games list. You maintain ownership of your current titles and when you purchase a new game it will still show up in your collection.

title: How to Set Up Steam Family Sharing (13 Steps) [2026]
snippet:
As of August 2026, Steam Families remains Valve’s current name for what most players still call Steam family sharing. It replaced two older, separate systems: the original Family Library Sharing (which let you authorize one other computer to play your library) and Family View (a basic parental content filter). Valve merged both into a single family-management workflow that handles library access, purchase approval, and screen-time controls from one place, according to Steam’s official Families [...] 1. Update the Steam client on every machine that will use the family library.
2. Confirm everyone joining has their own Steam account and is on your friends list.
3. Open Family Management: Steam > Settings > Family, your display name > Account Details > Family Management, or store.steampowered.com/account in a browser.
4. Select Create a Family (or Join a Family if one already exists) and give it a name.
5. Invite each member and choose Adult or Child right on the invite screen. [...] Family Management includes a scheduling control for when a child-role account is allowed to launch games at all, separate from parental content filtering. Set windows for allowed play (for example, blocking weekday mornings before school) and Steam enforces it client-side, preventing game launches outside the configured hours rather than just logging the activity for you to review later.
